My thoughts:

1.) Assuming this is a Single Chip (everything on the same chip as in no circuit board) ChipSat the power requirements to operate it continually for the 22 year trip (4.367 light years / .2 c) would be well above any current battery technology that is both small and light (ie Lithium Ion Batteries). The only possible power source I could think of that would last would be a very damn small Plutonium Reactor with only a few grams of Plutonium. It would have to be about the size of a pack of cigarettes and weigh under 1 pound to make the whole concept feasible.

2.) Why cap it at .2 C? If the light sail is so small that it can't be targeted from Earth to propel the ship faster than that then why not make the light sail larger. Light sails can be manufactured out of extremely light materials so that a 100' diameter sail would only weigh a few pounds. They should be able to travel at least .5C without too much trouble in modifying the design.

3.) An optical data transmission from these back to Earth would take over 4 years once they reached Alpha Centauri with no certainty we would even receive the transmissions. If they launch a dozen or so of these every few weeks and they are all networked together so that they relay the data from microsat to microsat back to Earth it would virtually ensure we received the data. It would still take over 4 years once the first probes reached Alpha Centauri for the data to reach Earth, but at least it would reach us.

4.) If we have the technology to do this then why can't we build a series of solar powered Lasers in Space (Earth Orbit or Near Earth Orbit) and then build a manned ship to send to Alpha Centauri. We could build the ship large enough that it carry a crew of 4-5 people as well as a Couple Solar Powered Lasers they could leave in the Alpha Centauri system to power them on a return voyage to Earth. You could send a group of exceptionally bright people on the trip, they could survey Alpha Centauri system using a small shuttle craft once there and then return to Earth in 30-40 years with an absolute wealth of information. Furthermore, if they were travelling each way at .5C the time dilation effect would have them only aging about 10 years while on Earth 30-40 years will pass. They could also take a series of small MicroSat's that are solar/solar wind powered and deploy them along the way so they could relay information back to Earth while they are gone. Truth be told I would even undertake such a voyage alone if given the opportunity.
